steps.prompt: Two builders are making a treehouse. Who finishes first?
steps.a: Builder A starts nailing boards right away. Halfway up, the boards don’t reach, the door is on the wrong side, and half the wood is used up.
steps.b: Builder B spends ten minutes drawing a plan: floor, walls, door, roof, how many boards each. Then B builds it in one go.
steps.reveal: An outline is your essay’s plan. Ten minutes of planning saves an hour of rewriting, and every paragraph ends up where it belongs.

cards.title: What goes in an outline
cards.body: One short line for each part: Hook, Thesis, then for each body paragraph its point (Body 1, Body 2, Body 3) and its Evidence, then the Conclusion. Notes, not full paragraphs: just enough to write from.

cards.title: An outline
cards.text:
Hook: What if every school had a garden?
Thesis: Every school should have a garden because gardens teach science, encourage healthy eating and bring students together.
Body 1: Gardens teach science.
Evidence: Students measure plant growth and test soil.
Body 2: Gardens encourage healthy eating.
Evidence: Kids are more likely to eat vegetables they grew themselves.
Body 3: Gardens bring students together.
Evidence: Our garden club has members from every grade.
Conclusion: A garden teaches, feeds and connects, so every school should plant one.
cards.note: Each body point matches one reason in the thesis: science, healthy eating, together.

cards.title: Your outline builder
cards.body: In the challenge, the outline builder gives you a box for each part, with sentence starters. Press “Put it in my writing” to turn the boxes into an outline, then check the Coach’s outline map: a ✓ for each part in place, a ! for each part to work on.

prompts: Look at your outline map. Does every body point link to your thesis?
Which body point has the strongest evidence? Which needs more?
